title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
description:
# Median of Two Sorted Arrays

Given two sorted integer arrays `nums1` and `nums2`, return the median of all values from both arrays.

The median is the middle value after the two arrays are conceptually merged. If the total number of values is even, the median is the average of the two middle values.

The required overall time complexity is `O(log (m + n))`, where `m = nums1.length` and `n = nums2.length`.

## Example 1

**Input:** nums1 = [1,3], nums2 = [2]

**Output:** 2.00000

**Explanation:** The merged order is [1,2,3], so the median is 2.

## Example 2

**Input:** nums1 = [1,2], nums2 = [3,4]

**Output:** 2.50000

**Explanation:** The merged order is [1,2,3,4], so the median is (2 + 3) / 2 = 2.5.

## Constraints

* `nums1.length == m`
* `nums2.length == n`
* `0 <= m <= 1000`
* `0 <= n <= 1000`
* `1 <= m + n <= 2000`
* `-1000000 <= nums1[i], nums2[i] <= 1000000`
* `nums1` and `nums2` are sorted in non-decreasing order.

tests.description: Unequal lengths with even total length
Negative and positive ranges with even total length
All negative values with odd total length
Median lands at the first value of the longer right side
Interleaved arrays with odd total length
Very uneven lengths with even total length
Minimum and maximum boundary values average to zero

solutions.name: Binary Partition on Shorter Array
solutions.description:
## Approach

Binary-search the cut position in the shorter array. The cut in the other array is determined by the requirement that the combined left half contains half of all values. When both left-side boundary values are less than or equal to both right-side boundary values, the partition is valid.

## Key Insight

A valid median partition has every value on the left side less than or equal to every value on the right side. Searching only the shorter array keeps boundary cases small and gives the optimal logarithmic complexity.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(log(min(m,n)))
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Recursive Kth Element Elimination
solutions.description:
## Approach

Reduce the median problem to finding the k-th smallest value. To find k, compare roughly the k/2-th remaining value of each array and discard the smaller prefix, because those discarded values cannot contain the k-th value.

## Key Insight

Each recursive step removes at least k/2 candidates while preserving the rank of the desired value in the remaining suffixes. The two median ranks are `(total + 1) / 2` and `(total + 2) / 2`, which also handles odd totals.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(log(m+n))
- Space Complexity: O(log(m+n))

solutions.name: Full Merge Baseline
solutions.description:
## Approach

Merge the two sorted arrays as in merge sort, then read the median from the merged array.

## Key Insight

This route does not meet the required logarithmic complexity, but it is the cleanest correctness baseline. It makes the median definition explicit before introducing the optimized partition and kth-element methods.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(m+n)
- Space Complexity: O(m+n)

solutions.name: Two Pointers to the Median Position
solutions.description:
## Approach

Advance two merge pointers only until the median position is reached. Track the previous and current selected values so even-length totals can average the two middle values.

## Key Insight

The median only depends on the middle one or two merged positions. This keeps the simple merge intuition while avoiding the full merged array allocation.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(m+n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)
